title: What If We Smashed a Spacecraft Into an Asteroid? NASA Did

scenes.text: What if we crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid on purpose? NASA did, seven million miles away.
In September 2022, the DART probe, about the size of a refrigerator, hit the moonlet Dimorphos.
It struck at roughly 14,000 miles an hour. Dimorphos is a 525-foot rock circling a bigger asteroid.
Before the hit, it circled its partner every 11 hours and 55 minutes.
Afterward, it took 11 hours and 23 minutes. The orbit got 32 minutes shorter.
NASA had hoped for a change of 73 seconds. It beat that by more than 25 times.

description:
What if we crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid?
NASA's DART mission did, and it shortened the asteroid's orbit by 32 minutes, more than 25 times the minimum goal.
